chapter.heading: Jonah Preaches at Nineveh
chapter.v:
Now the
word of the Lord came to Jonah the second time, saying, [Rom. 3:8; 6:15]

“Arise, go
to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the message that I tell you.” [[Rom. 6:11; 7:4, 6; Gal. 2:19; Col. 2:20; 3:3]; 1 Pet.]

So Jonah
arose and went to Nineveh, according to the word of the Lord. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, a three-day journey in extent. [Acts 2:38; 8:16; 19:5; [Gal. 3:27]; Col. 2:12 d [1 Cor. ed here. In Adam, we all sinned (see 1 Cor. 15:22). The result]

And Jonah
began to enter the city on the first day’s walk. Then he cried out and said, “Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!”The People of Nineveh Believe [Col. 2:12 f 1 Cor. 6:14 g John 2:11 h Rom. 7:6; [2 Cor. 5:17; Gal. 6:15; Eph. 4:23; Col. 3:10]]

So the
people of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least of them. [2 Cor. 4:10; Phil. 3:10; Col. 2:12; 3:1]

Then word
came to the king of Nineveh; and he arose from his throne and laid aside his robe, covered himself with sackcloth and sat in ashes. [Gal. 2:20; 5:24; 6:14 k Col.]

And he
caused it to be proclaimed and published throughout Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying,Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything; do not let them eat, or drink water. [1 Pet. 4:1]

But let
man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily to God; yes, let every one turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands. [Rom. 6:4; 2 Cor. 4:10; 2 Tim.]

Who can
tell if God will turn and relent, and turn away from His fierce anger, so that we may not perish? [Rev. 1:18]

Then God
saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God relented from the disaster that He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not do it. [Heb. 9:27] [Luke 20:38]
